_about: answer = index of the right option (shuffled on screen); evidence = supporting sentence, review only; hint = gentle "look again" line.

rabbit-hole.q: What did the White Rabbit take out of his waistcoat-pocket?
rabbit-hole.evidence: I shall be late!” (when she thought it over afterwards, it occurred to her that she ought to have wondered at this, but at the time it all seemed quite natural); but when the Rabbit actually took a watch out of its waistcoat-pocket, and looked at it, and then hurried on, Alice started to her feet
rabbit-hole.hint: Look again at the very start, when Alice first sees the Rabbit.

rabbit-hole.q: Why didn’t Alice drop the empty marmalade jar as she fell?
options: She was afraid of killing somebody below
She wanted to keep it for later
It was stuck to her hand
rabbit-hole.evidence: it was labelled “Orange Marmalade,” but to her great disappointment it was empty: she did not like to drop the jar for fear of killing somebody
rabbit-hole.hint: Look again at the part where Alice takes a jar down from a shelf.

rabbit-hole.q: Before drinking from the “Drink Me” bottle, Alice checks if it says “poison”. What does this show?
options: She was being sensible and careful
She didn’t like the taste of things
She wanted to save it for someone else
rabbit-hole.evidence: “No, I’ll look first,” she said, “and see whether it’s marked ‘poison’ or not”
rabbit-hole.hint: Look again at the part where Alice finds the little bottle.

pool.q: What was the pool that Alice found herself swimming in?
options: The tears she had cried when she was nine feet high
The sea, near a railway station
pool.evidence: However, she soon made out that she was in the pool of tears which she had wept when she was nine feet high.
pool.hint: Look again at the part where Alice thinks she has fallen into the sea.

pool.q: Why did Alice cry so much in the hall?
options: She was too big to get through the little door into the garden
The White Rabbit was rude to her
pool.evidence: It was as much as she could do, lying down on one side, to look through into the garden with one eye; but to get through was more hopeless than ever: she sat down and began to cry again.
pool.hint: Look again at the part where Alice grows very tall.

pool.q: Alice asks herself, “Who in the world am I?” Why does she feel so mixed up?
options: So many strange things have happened that she isn’t sure she’s the same girl
She has forgotten her own name for fun
Someone has told her she is a different girl
pool.evidence: But if I’m not the same, the next question is, Who in the world am I?
pool.hint: Look again at the part where Alice wonders if she has been changed in the night.

caucus.q: What prize did Alice get at the end of the Caucus-race?
caucus.evidence: Then they all crowded round her once more, while the Dodo solemnly presented the thimble
caucus.hint: Look again at the part where everyone asks who will give the prizes.

caucus.q: Why did the Dodo suggest a Caucus-race?
options: To get away from the Mouse
caucus.evidence: “What I was going to say,” said the Dodo in an offended tone, “was, that the best thing to get us dry would be a Caucus-race.”
caucus.hint: Look again at what everyone wanted after climbing out of the pool.

caucus.q: The Dodo says “everybody has won”. What is funny about this race?
options: A race where everyone wins isn’t really a race at all
caucus.evidence: At last the Dodo said, “everybody has won, and all must have prizes.”
caucus.hint: Look again at what the Dodo says when everyone asks who has won.

rabbit-house.q: What did the White Rabbit call Alice when he mistook her for someone else?
rabbit-house.evidence: Very soon the Rabbit noticed Alice, as she went hunting about, and called out to her in an angry tone, “Why, Mary Ann, what are you doing out here?
rabbit-house.hint: Look again at the start of the chapter, when the Rabbit is hunting for his fan and gloves.

rabbit-house.q: Why did Alice get stuck in the White Rabbit’s house?
options: She drank from a bottle and grew too big
Bill the Lizard sat on her
rabbit-house.evidence: She hastily put down the bottle, saying to herself “That’s quite enough—I hope I shan’t grow any more—As it is, I can’t get out at the door—I do wish I hadn’t drunk quite so much!”
rabbit-house.hint: Look again at the part where Alice finds a bottle in the Rabbit’s room.

rabbit-house.q: The pebbles thrown at Alice turn into little cakes. Why does this give her a “bright idea”?
options: Eating a cake might change her size and let her get out
She was hungry and wanted a snack
She could throw the cakes back
rabbit-house.evidence: Alice noticed with some surprise that the pebbles were all turning into little cakes as they lay on the floor, and a bright idea came into her head.
rabbit-house.hint: Look again at what happens to the pebbles on the floor.

caterpillar.q: What did the Caterpillar say the two sides of the mushroom would do?
options: One makes you grow taller, the other shorter
One makes you fly, the other swim
One sends you home, the other keeps you here
caterpillar.evidence: One side will make you grow taller, and the other side will make you grow shorter.
caterpillar.hint: Look again at what the Caterpillar says as it crawls away.

caterpillar.q: Why couldn’t Alice answer when the Caterpillar asked, “Who are you?”
options: She had changed so many times that day
She was too scared to speak
caterpillar.evidence: Alice replied, rather shyly, “I—I hardly know, sir, just at present—at least I know who I was when I got up this morning, but I think I must have been changed several times since then.”
caterpillar.hint: Look again at Alice’s first answer to the Caterpillar.

caterpillar.q: Alice calls three inches “a wretched height”, and the Caterpillar is angry. Why?
options: The Caterpillar is exactly three inches high
The Caterpillar wanted to be taller
Alice was rude about its mushroom
caterpillar.evidence: “It is a very good height indeed!” said the Caterpillar angrily, rearing itself upright as it spoke (it was exactly three inches high).
caterpillar.hint: Look again at how tall the Caterpillar is.

pepper.q: What did the Duchess’s baby turn into?
pepper.hint: Look again at the part where Alice carries the baby outside.

pepper.q: Why was everyone in the Duchess’s kitchen sneezing?
options: There was too much pepper in the soup
The kitchen was full of dust
pepper.evidence: “There’s certainly too much pepper in that soup!”
pepper.hint: Look again at what Alice says as she sneezes in the kitchen.

pepper.q: Alice asks why the cat grins. The Duchess says, “It’s a Cheshire cat, and that’s why.” Is that a real reason?
options: No — it doesn’t really explain anything
pepper.evidence: “It’s a Cheshire cat,” said the Duchess, “and that’s why.
pepper.hint: Look again at the Duchess’s answer about the cat.

tea-party.q: What time is it always at the Mad Tea-Party?
tea-party.hint: Look again at what the Hatter says about Time.

tea-party.q: Why is it always the same time at the tea-party?
tea-party.evidence: “We quarrelled last March—just before he went mad, you know—”
tea-party.hint: Look again at the Hatter’s story about the Queen’s concert.

tea-party.q: When the Hatter wants a clean cup, what does everyone do?
options: They all move one place on round the table
tea-party.evidence: “I want a clean cup,” interrupted the Hatter: “let’s all move one place on.”
tea-party.hint: Look again at what the Hatter says when he wants a clean cup.

croquet.q: What were used as the croquet balls and mallets?
croquet.evidence: the balls were live hedgehogs, the mallets live flamingoes
croquet.hint: Look again at Alice’s first look at the croquet-ground.

croquet.q: Why were the gardeners painting the roses red?
options: They had planted a white rose-tree by mistake
Red was the King’s favourite colour
croquet.evidence: Two began in a low voice, “Why the fact is, you see, Miss, this here ought to have been a red rose-tree, and we put a white one in by mistake; and if the Queen was to find it out, we should all have our heads cut off, you know.
croquet.hint: Look again at what the gardener tells Alice.

croquet.q: The Queen screams “Off with her head!” and Alice says “Nonsense!” — and the Queen goes quiet. What does this show?
options: Standing up to someone who shouts can work
croquet.evidence: “Nonsense!” said Alice, very loudly and decidedly, and the Queen was silent.
croquet.hint: Look again at the part where the Queen first meets Alice.

mock-turtle.q: Who took Alice to see the Mock Turtle?
mock-turtle.evidence: “Up, lazy thing!” said the Queen, “and take this young lady to see the Mock Turtle, and to hear his history.
mock-turtle.hint: Look again at the part where they find someone asleep in the sun.

mock-turtle.q: Why did the Mock Turtle say they called their teacher “Tortoise”?
options: Because he lived in a shell
mock-turtle.evidence: “We called him Tortoise because he taught us,” said the Mock Turtle angrily
mock-turtle.hint: Look again at the Mock Turtle’s school days.

mock-turtle.q: The Gryphon says lessons are called lessons “because they lessen from day to day”. What kind of joke is this?
mock-turtle.evidence: “That’s the reason they’re called lessons,” the Gryphon remarked: “because they lessen from day to day.”
mock-turtle.hint: Look again at what Alice asks about hours of lessons.

quadrille.q: In the Lobster Quadrille, who is each dancer’s partner?
quadrille.evidence: “Each with a lobster as a partner!” cried the Gryphon.
quadrille.hint: Look again at how the Gryphon explains the dance.

quadrille.q: In the song, why does the whiting ask the snail to walk faster?
options: A porpoise is close behind, treading on his tail
The dance is about to start
quadrille.evidence: ‘There’s a porpoise close behind us, and he’s treading on my tail.
quadrille.hint: Look again at the first lines of the song.

quadrille.q: Alice says it was “a very interesting dance to watch” and is glad it’s over. What does this tell us?
options: She wanted to see it again straight away
She thought it was too short
quadrille.evidence: “Thank you, it’s a very interesting dance to watch,” said Alice, feeling very glad that it was over at last
quadrille.hint: Look again at what Alice says when the dance ends.

tarts.q: What is the Knave of Hearts accused of?
tarts.evidence: The Knave of Hearts, he stole those tarts,
tarts.hint: Look again at what the White Rabbit reads out from his scroll.

tarts.q: Why did the Dormouse complain about Alice in the court?
options: She was growing larger and squashing him
tarts.evidence: “I can’t help it,” said Alice very meekly: “I’m growing.”
tarts.hint: Look again at the curious feeling Alice has in the court.

tarts.q: There is a dish of tarts on the table in the middle of the court. What does that suggest?
options: Maybe the tarts were never really stolen
tarts.evidence: In the very middle of the court was a table, with a large dish of tarts upon it
tarts.hint: Look again at what Alice sees when she arrives at the court.

vault.q: How did Alice first get into Wonderland?
options: She followed the White Rabbit down a rabbit-hole
She fell asleep on a train
vault.evidence: it flashed across her mind that she had never before seen a rabbit with either a waistcoat-pocket, or a watch to take out of it
vault.hint: Think back to the very first chapter.

vault.q: What helped Alice get small enough to escape from the Rabbit’s house?
vault.evidence: Alice noticed with some surprise that the pebbles were all turning into little cakes as they lay on the floor
vault.hint: Think about what the pebbles turned into.

vault.q: The Queen says “Sentence first—verdict afterwards.” What is wrong with that?
options: You should decide if someone is guilty before you punish them
vault.hint: Think about what a trial is for.

vault.q: When does Alice finally stand up to the whole court?
options: When she has grown to her full size
When she is three inches tall
vault.evidence: “Who cares for you?” said Alice, (she had grown to her full size by this time.)
vault.hint: Think about Alice’s size at the end of the trial.

vault.q: What did Alice call the King, the Queen and their court?
options: Nothing but a pack of cards
vault.evidence: “You’re nothing but a pack of cards!”
vault.hint: Think about how the trial ends.

vault.q: Where was Alice when she woke up?
options: On the bank, with her head in her sister’s lap
At the bottom of the rabbit-hole
vault.evidence: she gave a little scream, half of fright and half of anger, and tried to beat them off, and found herself lying on the bank, with her head in the lap of her sister
vault.hint: Think about the very last chapter.

vault.q: What did all of Alice’s adventures turn out to be?
options: A story her sister told her
vault.evidence: “Oh, I’ve had such a curious dream!” said Alice
vault.hint: Think about what Alice tells her sister.
